scope: What the Indian state did under FCRA 2010 from 2011 to 2026: aggregate cancellation and cessation counts (Parliament answers and MHA-portal figures as relayed by press, because fcraonline.nic.in and mha.gov.in are blocked from this environment), the FCRA Amendment Act 2020 provision by provision with cui-bono rows and its Supreme Court test (Noel Harper, 2022-04-08), and 22 case files — suspensions, refusals, cancellations, restorations, court orders — each with the order date, the stated ground as an alleged claim, the association's response as a contra, and supersession where an order was reversed. Covers UPA-era controls (Kudankulam 2012, CPSC 2012–14, INSAF 2013) and non-critic controls (Missionaries of Charity, World Vision, CASA, EFI, CARE, Bal Raksha Bharat) with the same fields. Leaves out: receipts by donor (other agent), government-aligned associations' receipts (other agent), the 2016/2018 Finance Act retrospective amendments (other agent), the 2011 Anna Hazare-era Ford Foundation discourse (no source opened — recorded as a gap), and any year-wise 2011–2026 cancellation table (void at source).

entities.label: FCRA 2010
entities.sub: Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010 — registration, prior permission, suspension (s.13), cancellation (s.14)
entities.publicRole: The statute under which every registration, refusal, suspension and cancellation in this file was made.
d: Cancellations 2011 → 2021-02-10: registration certificates of more than 20,600 associations cancelled; MHA said most were for non-filing of annual returns (Lok Sabha written reply, MoS Home Nityanand Rai, 2021-02-10) [documented]
Cancellations 2018–2020: 1,810 (same reply) [documented]
Registered associations, 2021-02: about 22,400; foreign contribution received 2016-17 to 2018-19: over ₹58,000 crore (same reply) [documented]
Cancellations 2018–2022: 1,827 for violations (Parliament reply, 2023-03, as cited by Tribune 2024-01-20) [documented]
Cancellations 2017–2021: 6,677 (Outlook 2023-09-15, citing MHA data) [reported]
Cancellations 2015–2024: more than 16,000 (Tribune 2024-01-20, citing MHA data) [reported]

2022-01-01 cessation event: 5,933 registrations "deemed to cease" — 5,789 did not apply for renewal despite reminders, 179 applications denied; active count fell from 22,762 to 16,829; these were among 18,778 registrations that expired between 2020-09-29 and 2021-12-31; 12,580 had ceased cumulatively in earlier years (ThePrint + Scroll, 2022-01-01, both citing the MHA portal) [documented]
Portal counts, 2024-05: active 16,242; expired 14,396; cancelled 20,701; foreign contribution received 2019–2022: ₹55,741.51 crore (The CSR Universe 2024-05-01, citing parliamentary data) [reported]

UPA-era count: 4,141 registrations cancelled in 2012–13 out of 39,236 registered; Tamil Nadu 794 (19%); 20 accounts frozen; 60 barred from applying (Hinduism Today HPI 2013-08-30, citing News Bharati — secondary aggregator, unverified against the MHA Annual Report) [reported — weak source]

narratives.claim: The Modi government uses FCRA to silence its critics.
narratives.strongestCase: A dated sequence of critics losing registration under stated grounds that reach content: Greenpeace (2015, after Delhi HC had called the fund-block arbitrary), Lawyers Collective (2016, protests as "political activities"), Sabrang (2016, the day before the Gulberg verdict), Navsarjan (2016, "harmony", five months after Una), CPSC (2016 refusal citing engagement with UN Special Rapporteurs), Amnesty (2020), CHRI (2021–22), Oxfam (2022, then a CBI FIR over lobbying foreign governments), RGF/RGCT (2022), CPR (2024, publication equated with current affairs), Environics (2024, protest payments). The 2020 Amendment then removed the intermediary model on which several of them ran.
narratives.strongestCounter: The overwhelming majority of the 20,000+ cancellations are for non-filing; the 2022-01-01 cessation was 97% non-application (5,789 of 5,968). The same period cancelled the largest Christian relief bodies (World Vision ₹170 crore; CASA; Compassion US$45m/yr), health NGOs (VHAI, Hemophilia Federation) and a Gandhi-family foundation on grounds identical in form. The UPA used the same grounds (INSAF 2013: transfers for protests; CPSC 2012–14; Kudankulam 2012 with the PM naming US/Scandinavian funders). Courts deferred: CHRI lost (2022-02-14); the Supreme Court upheld the regime (2022-04-08).
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: A year-wise MHA table of grounds: if content-based grounds (s.3, "harmony", "economic interests") fall on advocacy bodies at a rate far above their share of the registered population, the narrative moves to well-supported; if the grounds distribution mirrors the population, it moves to speculative.

symmetryCheck: UPA (2011–14) against NDA (2014–26): the UPA-era record reachable here shows the same instrument used the same way — INSAF suspended 2013-04-30 on an onward-transfer-for-protests ground and quashed as premature and unreasoned; CPSC/People's Watch suspended three times 2012–14 and vindicated in 2014-03; three Kudankulam-area associations cancelled 2012-02 with the Prime Minister naming US and Scandinavian funders; a weakly-sourced 4,141 cancellations in 2012-13. The NDA-era record adds scale (20,600 cancellations by 2021, mostly non-filing; 5,933 cessations on one day in 2022), the 2020 statute, and a longer list of named critics — but the same lens on non-critics produces Missionaries of Charity (refused, restored), World Vision (₹170 crore), CASA, EFI, Compassion (US$45m/yr), CARE India (₹377.5 crore), Bal Raksha Bharat (₹163 crore), VHAI, Hemophilia Federation, Institute of Economic Growth. Government-aligned associations (VIF, India Foundation, Ekal/Vidya Bharati affiliates) were not examined in this file — they belong to the receipts agent; the absence of any recorded enforcement against them is a question for that file, not a finding of this one. Courts: under both governments the High Courts struck MHA on procedure (2013, 2014, 2015); after the 2020 Amendment they deferred (CHRI 2022; Noel Harper 2022).
